### 2. Minimal Submanifolds in Spheres
A minimal submanifold is a critical point of the area functional. In the context of spheres $\mathbb{S}^N$, a well-known result regarding minimal submanifolds is the **existence of minimal submanifolds of the form $\mathbb{S}^k \times \mathbb{S}^l$** (products of spheres) embedded in larger spheres.

Specifically, the product of two spheres $\mathbb{S}^k \times \mathbb{S}^l$ can be embedded minimally into $\mathbb{S}^{k+l+2}$. This is achieved by the "product construction" where one takes the intersection of $\mathbb{S}^{k+1}$ and $\mathbb{S}^{l+1}$ inside $\mathbb{S}^{k+l+2}$, or more formally, by considering the set of points in $\mathbb{R}^{k+1} \oplus \mathbb{R}^{l+1} \oplus \mathbb{R}$ satisfying the sphere equation, which yields a minimal submanifold. The dimension of this submanifold is $k+l$, and the ambient dimension is $k+l+2$.
